data.claim: A signal-killed review records the finished chunks (bug B982d306cc8) but a re-run re-sends EVERY chunk. Checkpointing the cut's identity (reviewer, diff_sha, chunks_total, max_chunk_chars) the moment the runner knows it lets the next run resume from the next unreviewed chunk of the SAME cut.
data.falsifier: The resumed run re-sends an already-reviewed chunk (the test asserts chunk 1's marker appears exactly once across both runs), or the partial record lacks diff_sha/chunks_total/reviewer so a resume cannot name the cut.
data.mechanism: ddflow/services/review/runner.review already computes diff_sha/chunks_total/max_chunk_chars after splitting the diff; wire an on_plan callback that writes one plan line into the reply file, surface it in the terminated gate's evidence, and have scope._scope resume via _resume_of_terminated, which reuses _rerun_scope to validate the cut matches before picking only the missing chunk numbers.

chunk_findings.detail: The test never inspects the actual finished chunk’s outcome/finding. After the first kill it checks only `evidence["reviewed"] == [1]`, and after resume it checks only `evidence["reviewed"] == [1, 2]` and that `x_marker_zz` was not re-sent. An implementation that checkpointed the chunk *index* `1` but discarded the replied `FINDING HIGH x.py:1` payload would satisfy every assertion, yet the gate would silently lose the x.py finding — the exact “persist each finished chunk’s outcome” behavior this test claims to pin. The test should assert the chunk-1 finding content is present after the kill and still present in the final gate after resume.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_checkpoint.py:test_a_killed_review_resumes_from_the_next_chunk

chunk_findings.detail: A rejected explicit chunk rerun is treated as “no rerun” and can be replaced by a terminated-run resume. After `if a["chunks"]`, a string from `_rerun_scope` is stored in `why` and `rerun` is set to `None`; the new `if rerun is None` then calls `_resume_of_terminated` with no check that `a["chunks"]` was empty and without clearing `why`. Given `a["chunks"] == [1]` and `_rerun_scope` returning an error (chunk 1 already reviewed, out of range, or otherwise not a valid rerun) while a PARTIAL record still has missing chunk 3 that `_rerun_scope` accepts, the function returns that error in `why` and a resume scope for chunk 3 in `rerun`. Callers that honor `rerun` review the wrong chunks; callers that honor `why` drop a resume the two-line-above contract (`rerun` set ⇒ `why` empty) no longer describes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/scope.py:_resume_of_terminated call site

chunk_findings.detail: `seen` is not reset between the kill and the resume, and the slow reviewer appends the chunk body before it sleeps. After a kill, `seen` already contains `y_marker_zz` from the terminated invocation, so `assert "y_marker_zz" in got` is true even when the second `review` never calls the reviewer. A resume that only rewrites `evidence["reviewed"]` to `[1, 2]` from the checkpoint (without sending chunk 2, and without re-sending `x_marker_zz`) satisfies every assert in `test_a_killed_review_resumes_from_the_next_chunk`, including `got.count("x_marker_zz") == 1`. The same log also never checks that chunk 1’s stored finding is still on the gate, so “keep the finished outcome” is untested.

chunk_findings.detail: The test verifies that the checkpointed `x.py` finding survives a resume, but it never verifies that the resumed chunk’s own `y.py` finding was persisted. After resume it builds `locs` from `chunk_findings` and asserts only `any(loc.startswith("x.py") for loc in locs)`. An implementation that marks chunk 2 as reviewed and sends its body (`"y_marker_zz" in got`) but drops the `FINDING HIGH y.py:1` output would still pass every assertion. That is the same index-without-finding data loss the test’s own comment calls out for chunk 1, left unpinned for chunk 2.

chunk_findings.detail: `wanted = prior.get("wanted") or list(range(1, total + 1))` treats a persisted empty `wanted` list as if the field were absent. Since `Reviewer.plan` now writes `wanted` as a list, an evidence record such as `{"chunks_total": 3, "reviewed": [], "wanted": []}` would fell back to `[1, 2, 3]`, so `missing` becomes every chunk. That widens the exact scope the new docstring says a resume must never widen. Distinguish “missing key” from “empty list” (for example `if "wanted" in prior`), or do not write empty `wanted` for no requested chunks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/scope.py:47

chunk_findings.detail: The cut identity is known as soon as `chunks` and `wanted` are computed, but `on_plan` now runs only after `files = [chunk_files(c) for c in chunks]`. `wanted` does not depend on `chunk_files`. A SIGKILL during that list comprehension leaves no plan line (`diff_sha`, `chunks_total`, `max_chunk_chars`, `wanted`), so `_resume_of_terminated` cannot match the cut and the next run re-reviews every chunk. The previous call sat above that loop, so the same kill still had a resumable checkpoint.
